source.text: וְעַתָּ֥ה שְׁמַ֖ע יַעֲקֹ֣ב עַבְדִּ֑י וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּחַ֥רְתִּי בֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And now hear, O Jacob, my servant, and Israel, [whom] I have chosen him.

en.L: But now hear, O Jacob, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant, and Israel, whom I have chosen.
en.B: But now listen, Jacob, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant, Israel, the one I have chosen.
en.R: But now, people of Israel, listen. You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant, the people I have chosen.

decisions.choice: and now: a turn from judgment to promise
decisions.reason: The words mark a fresh start after 43:22-28, where Israel's sins brought ruin. The same turn opens 43:1.

decisions.choice: my servant: the people of Israel, called to serve God
decisions.reason: Here the servant is named as Jacob and Israel, the whole people (41:8-9; 44:21). The servant is not described as a slave but as someone God has chosen and keeps.

decisions.choice: people of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable shows that Jacob and Israel name the whole people here, not the ancestor.

source.text: כֹּה־אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֥ה עֹשֶׂ֛ךָ וְיֹצֶרְךָ֥ מִבֶּ֖טֶן יַעְזְרֶ֑ךָּ אַל־תִּירָא֙ עַבְדִּ֣י יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וִישֻׁר֖וּן בָּחַ֥רְתִּי בֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says [the] LORD, [who] made you and formed you from [the] womb, he will help you: do not be afraid, my servant Jacob, and Jeshurun [whom] I have chosen him.

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who made you and formed you from [the] womb, [who] will help you: Do not be afraid, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Jacob, and Jeshurun, whom I have chosen.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this, he who made you, who shaped you in the womb and will come to your aid: Have no fear, Jacob, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant, Jeshurun, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} chosen one.
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says. He made you. He formed you before you were born, and he will help you. He says: Do not be afraid, people of Israel. You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant. You are Jeshurun, the people I have chosen.

decisions.choice: Jeshurun: a name of honor for Israel, probably meaning 'the upright one'
decisions.reason: The name appears elsewhere only in Deuteronomy 32:15; 33:5, 26. It seems to come from the word for 'upright', a fond name for the people as God means them to be. Its exact sense is not certain, so the name itself is kept.

decisions.choice: formed you from the womb: God shaped Israel from its very beginning
decisions.reason: The people are pictured as a child God formed before birth (44:24; 49:1, 5). It speaks of God's care from the nation's first days.

decisions.choice: You are Jeshurun
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the name but makes clear that it is another name for God's people.

source.text: כִּ֤י אֶצָּק־מַ֨יִם֙ עַל־צָמֵ֔א וְנֹזְלִ֖ים עַל־יַבָּשָׁ֑ה אֶצֹּ֤ק רוּחִי֙ עַל־זַרְעֶ֔ךָ וּבִרְכָתִ֖י עַל־צֶאֱצָאֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: For I will pour water on thirsty [land] and streams on dry ground; I will pour my Spirit on your offspring, and my blessing on your descendants.

en.L: For I will pour water on [the] thirsty [land], and streams on [the] dry ground; I will pour {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Spirit on your offspring, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} blessing on your descendants.
en.B: For I will pour out water on parched ground and send streams across the dry land; I will pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Spirit on your children, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} blessing on those who come after you.
en.R: I will pour water on the thirsty land. I will make streams flow over dry ground. In the same way I will pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Spirit on your children. I will bless your children's children.

decisions.choice: my Spirit: God's own Spirit, giving new life to the people
decisions.reason: Water on dry land is the picture; the Spirit poured out is what it means. God promises his life-giving presence to the next generations (32:15; Ezekiel 39:29; Joel 3:1). The same verb 'pour' is used for water and Spirit.

decisions.choice: thirsty: the parched land, or perhaps a thirsty person
decisions.reason: The word means 'thirsty' and has no noun. Set beside 'dry ground' it most likely means the thirsty land.

decisions.choice: In the same way
decisions.reason: Readable shows that the water in the first half is a picture of the Spirit in the second half.

source.text: וְצָמְח֖וּ בְּבֵ֣ין חָצִ֑יר כַּעֲרָבִ֖ים עַל־יִבְלֵי־מָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they will spring up in between grass, like poplars by channels of water.

en.L: And they will spring up among [the] grass, like poplars by channels of water.
en.B: They will shoot up among the grass like poplars beside running streams.
en.R: Your children will sprout up among the grass. They will grow like tall trees beside streams of water.

decisions.choice: among the grass: the reading of the Hebrew text is kept
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says they will spring up 'in between grass'. The Septuagint has 'like grass among water' (described from memory; reviewer to check), which supposes a slightly different text. The Hebrew makes sense as it stands: the new generation springs up in a land that has turned green.

decisions.choice: poplars: trees that grow along watercourses
decisions.reason: The word names a tree of riverbanks, probably the Euphrates poplar, often called a willow (Psalm 137:2). It pictures quick, strong growth where there is water.

decisions.choice: Your children
decisions.reason: Readable names who will spring up: the offspring of verse 3.

source.text: זֶ֤ה יֹאמַר֙ לַֽיהוָ֣ה אָ֔נִי וְזֶ֖ה יִקְרָ֣א בְשֵֽׁם־יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְזֶ֗ה יִכְתֹּ֤ב יָדוֹ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וּבְשֵׁ֥ם יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יְכַנֶּֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: This [one] will say, 'To [the] LORD I [belong],' and this [one] will call by the name of Jacob, and this [one] will write [on] his hand, 'To [the] LORD,' and by the name of Israel will take a title.

en.L: This one will say, "I [belong] to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}," and that one will call [himself] by the name of Jacob, and another will write [on] his hand, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}'s," and will be titled by the name of Israel.
en.B: One will say, "I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s"; another will claim the name of Jacob; another will write on the hand, "Belonging to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}," and take Israel as a name of honor.
en.R: One person will say, "I belong to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}." Another will use the name of Jacob. Another will write on their hand, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}'s." Another will proudly take the name Israel.

decisions.choice: write on his hand: a mark of belonging, as a slave or soldier might bear his master's name
decisions.reason: The words can also mean 'write with his hand', that is, sign his name as belonging to the LORD. A written mark on the hand showing whose a person is fits the picture of people joining God's people (compare 49:16, where God has Zion engraved on his palms).

decisions.choice: this one ... this one ... this one: different people joining God's people one by one
decisions.reason: The repeated 'this one' describes one person after another. They may be Israel's own children (verse 3) or people from other nations who join Israel (56:3-8); the verse does not say which.

decisions.choice: take a title: adopt Israel as an honored name
decisions.reason: The verb means to give someone a name of honor (45:4). Here the person takes the name Israel for himself.

source.text: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֧ה מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל וְגֹאֲל֖וֹ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת אֲנִ֤י רִאשׁוֹן֙ וַאֲנִ֣י אַחֲר֔וֹן וּמִבַּלְעָדַ֖י אֵ֥ין אֱלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says [the] LORD, [the] King of Israel and its Redeemer, [the] LORD of hosts: I [am the] first and I [am the] last, and besides me there is no god.

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the King of Israel and its Redeemer, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: I [am the] first and I [am the] last, and except for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} there is no god.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the King of Israel, its Redeemer, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, says this: I am the first and I am the last; there is no god but {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is the King of Israel. He is the one who rescues it. He is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. This is what he says: I am the first, and I am the last. There is no other god. There is only {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: the first and the last: God was there before all things and will be there at the end
decisions.reason: God alone stands at the beginning and the end of history (41:4; 48:12). In Revelation 1:17 and 22:13 Jesus speaks these words of himself.

decisions.choice: Redeemer: the relative who buys back and defends a family member
decisions.reason: A redeemer in Israel's law was a near relative who freed a kinsman from debt or slavery and stood up for him (Leviticus 25:25, 47-49). God takes this role for his people (41:14; 43:14).

decisions.choice: there is no god besides me: there is no other god at all
decisions.reason: The claim is not only that Israel should worship one God, but that no other god exists (45:5-6, 21). Verses 9-20 show what the idols really are.

source.text: וּמִֽי־כָמ֣וֹנִי יִקְרָ֗א וְיַגִּידֶ֤הָ וְיַעְרְכֶ֨הָ֙ לִ֔י מִשּׂוּמִ֖י עַם־עוֹלָ֑ם וְאֹתִיּ֛וֹת וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר תָּבֹ֖אנָה יַגִּ֥ידוּ לָֽמוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And who [is] like me? Let him call, and let him declare it and set it in order for me, since I established [the] people of antiquity; and [the] coming [things] and what will come, let them declare to them.

en.L: And who [is] like {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? Let him proclaim [it], and let him declare it and set it in order for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, since I established the ancient people; and the things coming, and what will come, let them declare to them.
en.B: Who can compare with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? Let him speak up, announce it, and set it out in order for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, from the day I founded the people of long ago. Let them make known what is coming, the things that are still to happen.
en.R: Is there anyone like {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? If there is, let him speak up. Let him explain to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} all that has happened since I made {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people long ago. Let the false gods tell what is going to happen in the future.

decisions.choice: since I established the ancient people: the challenge reaches back to the beginning of Israel
alternatives: who announced from long ago the things to come
decisions.reason: The rival is dared to tell all that has happened from the time God made his people long ago. Some have proposed a small change in the letters to read 'who announced from of old the things to come', which fits the next line, but the Hebrew text as it stands makes sense.

decisions.choice: let them declare to them: let the rival gods tell their followers
decisions.reason: 'Them' most likely means the idols' worshipers. A change of one letter would give 'to us', which some prefer (41:22-23).

decisions.choice: who is like me: a courtroom challenge to the other gods
decisions.reason: As in 41:21-29 and 43:9, God calls the gods to prove they are gods by telling the past and foretelling the future. None can.

decisions.choice: the false gods; my people
decisions.reason: Readable names who 'they' are and makes clear that the ancient people is Israel.

source.text: אַֽל־תִּפְחֲדוּ֙ וְאַל־תִּרְה֔וּ הֲלֹ֥א מֵאָ֛ז הִשְׁמַעְתִּ֥יךָ וְהִגַּ֖דְתִּי וְאַתֶּ֣ם עֵדָ֑י הֲיֵ֤שׁ אֱל֨וֹהַּ֙ מִבַּלְעָדַ֔י וְאֵ֥ין צ֖וּר בַּל־יָדָֽעְתִּי׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not be in dread and do not fear; have I not from then made you hear and declared, and you [are] my witnesses? Is there a god besides me? And there is no rock; I do not know [one].

en.L: Do not be in dread, and do not fear. Did I not from of old make you hear and declare [it]? And you [are] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} witnesses! Is there a god except for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? And there is no Rock; I know [of] none.
en.B: Do not shake with dread or be afraid. Did I not announce it to you long ago and make it known? You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} witnesses. Is there any god apart from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? There is no other Rock; I know of none.
en.R: Do not be frightened. Do not be afraid. Long ago I told you what would happen. I announced it. You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} witnesses. Is there any other god besides {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? There is no other Rock. I do not know of any.

decisions.choice: Rock: a name for God as the one who is firm and gives shelter
decisions.reason: God is called the Rock of Israel (17:10; 26:4; 30:29; Deuteronomy 32:4, 31). He alone is a sure place of safety.

decisions.choice: I know of none: God himself knows of no other god
decisions.reason: The one who knows all things says there is no other. It is a strong denial, not a sign that God lacks knowledge.

decisions.choice: you are my witnesses: Israel can testify that God foretold events
decisions.reason: The people have heard God announce things before they happened and can bear witness to it (43:10, 12).

source.text: יֹֽצְרֵי־פֶ֤סֶל כֻּלָּם֙ תֹּ֔הוּ וַחֲמוּדֵיהֶ֖ם בַּל־יוֹעִ֑ילוּ וְעֵדֵיהֶ֣ם הֵׄ֗מָּׄהׄבַּל־יִרְא֛וּ וּבַל־יֵדְע֖וּ לְמַ֥עַן יֵבֹֽשׁוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: [Those who] form an idol, all of them [are] emptiness, and their delights do not profit; and their witnesses, they do not see and do not know, so that they may be ashamed.

en.L: [Those who] form an idol, all of them [are] emptiness, and the things they delight in do not profit; and their witnesses, they neither see nor know, so that they will be put to shame.
en.B: All who shape idols are nothing, and the things they love do them no good. Their own witnesses see nothing and know nothing, so that they will be put to shame.
en.R: People who make idols are worth nothing. The idols they love so much cannot help them. Those who speak up for the idols are blind and know nothing. So they will be put to shame.

decisions.choice: emptiness: something without substance or worth
decisions.reason: The word describes the formless earth in Genesis 1:2 and what is futile and empty (40:17, 23; 41:29). The idol makers come to nothing, like their idols.

decisions.choice: their witnesses: the idols' worshipers, or the idols themselves
decisions.reason: In contrast to Israel, God's witnesses (verse 8), the idols' witnesses can neither see nor know. They are probably the people who speak up for the idols, though the idols are also blind (verse 18). In the Hebrew text the word 'they' here carries special scribal dots (described from memory; reviewer to check), which may mark it as doubtful.

decisions.choice: so that they will be put to shame: the result of their blindness
decisions.reason: The words state the outcome: those who trust idols end in shame (42:17; 45:16).

decisions.choice: Those who speak up for the idols
decisions.reason: Readable explains who the witnesses are.

source.text: מִֽי־יָצַ֥ר אֵ֖ל וּפֶ֣סֶל נָסָ֑ךְ לְבִלְתִּ֖י הוֹעִֽיל׃

records.literal_gloss: Who has formed a god and an idol has cast, so as not to profit?

en.L: Who has formed a god and cast an idol [that is] of no profit?
en.B: Who would shape a god or cast an idol that brings no gain?
en.R: Who would make a god or pour metal into a mold to make an idol that cannot help anyone?

decisions.choice: who has formed: a question that mocks
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer that only a fool would do it. It is not a request for information.

decisions.choice: cast an idol: melt metal and pour it into a mold
decisions.reason: Idols were carved from wood or cast in metal and often overlaid with gold or silver (40:19-20).

source.text: הֵ֤ן כָּל־חֲבֵרָיו֙ יֵבֹ֔שׁוּ וְחָרָשִׁ֥ים הֵ֖מָּה מֵֽאָדָ֑ם יִֽתְקַבְּצ֤וּ כֻלָּם֙ יַֽעֲמֹ֔דוּ יִפְחֲד֖וּ יֵבֹ֥שׁוּ יָֽחַד׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, all his companions will be ashamed, and [the] craftsmen, they [are] from humankind; let them gather together, all of them, let them stand, let them be in dread, let them be ashamed together.

en.L: Look, all his companions will be put to shame, and the craftsmen, they [are] from humankind. Let them all gather together; let them stand up; they will be in dread; they will be put to shame together.
en.B: Look, all who join with it will be put to shame; its makers are only human. Let them all assemble and stand up; they will be filled with dread and put to shame together.
en.R: Everyone who worships that idol will be put to shame. The people who make idols are only human. Let them all come together and stand up in court. They will be terrified and put to shame.

decisions.choice: his companions: those joined to the idol, or to its maker
decisions.reason: The word means 'partners' or 'associates'. 'His' may refer to the idol of verse 10, whose worshipers are joined to it (Hosea 4:17), or to the one who makes it, whose fellow craftsmen share his shame.

decisions.choice: they are from humankind: mere human beings
decisions.reason: The craftsmen are only people; they cannot make a god.

decisions.choice: let them gather, let them stand: a summons to a trial
decisions.reason: As in 41:1 and 43:9, the idol makers are called to court to make their case. They will not be able to.

decisions.choice: stand up in court
decisions.reason: Readable makes the courtroom picture clear.

source.text: חָרַ֤שׁ בַּרְזֶל֙ מַֽעֲצָ֔ד וּפָעַל֙ בַּפֶּחָ֔ם וּבַמַּקָּב֖וֹת יִצְּרֵ֑הוּ וַיִּפְעָלֵ֨הוּ֙ בִּזְר֣וֹעַ כֹּח֔וֹ גַּם־רָעֵב֙ וְאֵ֣ין כֹּ֔חַ לֹא־שָׁ֥תָה מַ֖יִם וַיִּיעָֽף׃

records.literal_gloss: A craftsman of iron, a tool, and works on charcoal, and with hammers forms it, and works it with the arm of his strength; also he is hungry and there is no strength; he does not drink water and grows weary.

en.L: A craftsman of iron [takes] a tool and works [it] over charcoal, and with hammers he forms it, and he works it with the strength of his arm. He also becomes hungry, and there is no strength; he does not drink water, and he grows weary.
en.B: The ironsmith takes his tool and works it over hot charcoal. He beats it into shape with hammers, working it with all the strength of his arm. Yet he gets hungry and his strength runs out; he has no water to drink and is worn out.
en.R: A blacksmith takes a tool and works the metal in the hot coals. He pounds it into shape with hammers. He uses all the strength in his arms. But he gets hungry and weak. If he does not drink water, he gets tired.

decisions.choice: a craftsman of iron, a tool: the line is very brief, and its exact sense is uncertain
alternatives: the ironsmith makes a cutting tool
decisions.reason: The words may mean that the smith takes a tool to work with, or that he makes a cutting tool. The rest of the verse shows him shaping metal over coals with hammers.

decisions.choice: he grows hungry and tired: the maker is weak, unlike the God who does not grow weary
decisions.reason: The man who makes a god runs out of strength if he skips a meal. The LORD, in contrast, never grows faint or weary (40:28-31).

source.text: חָרַ֣שׁ עֵצִים֮ נָ֣טָה קָו֒ יְתָאֲרֵ֣הוּ בַשֶּׂ֔רֶד יַעֲשֵׂ֨הוּ֙ בַּמַּקְצֻע֔וֹת וּבַמְּחוּגָ֖ה יְתָאֳרֵ֑הוּ וַֽיַּעֲשֵׂ֨הוּ֙ כְּתַבְנִ֣ית אִ֔ישׁ כְּתִפְאֶ֥רֶת אָדָ֖ם לָשֶׁ֥בֶת בָּֽיִת׃

records.literal_gloss: A craftsman of woods stretches a line, outlines it with a marker, works it with planes, and with a compass outlines it, and made it like the form of a man, like the beauty of a human, to dwell [in] a house.

en.L: A craftsman of wood stretches out a line; he marks it out with a stylus; he works it with planes, and with a compass he marks it out; and he makes it like the form of a man, like the beauty of a human, to dwell [in] a house.
en.B: The woodworker stretches out a measuring line and sketches the shape with a stylus. He carves it with planes and marks it out with a compass. He makes it in the shape of a man, as handsome as any human, to sit in a house.
en.R: A woodworker measures a piece of wood with a line. He draws an outline on it with a marker. He shapes it with his tools and marks it with a compass. He carves it into the shape of a person, as good-looking as any human. Then he sets it up in a house.

decisions.choice: stylus, planes: woodworking tools whose exact kind is uncertain
decisions.reason: Both words occur only here. One was a tool for marking lines (a stylus, a scribing point, or chalk); the other was a tool for shaving or carving wood (planes or chisels).

decisions.choice: like the form of a man: the idol is shaped like its maker
decisions.reason: The craftsman makes a god in human shape. The irony is that God made humans in his image (Genesis 1:26-27), while here a human makes a god in his own.

decisions.choice: to dwell in a house: to stay in a shrine or a home
decisions.reason: The word 'house' can mean a temple or shrine, or a private home where household gods were kept (Judges 17:4-5). Either way the idol just sits where it is put (46:7).

source.text: לִכְרָת־ל֣וֹ אֲרָזִ֔ים וַיִּקַּ֤ח תִּרְזָה֙ וְאַלּ֔וֹן וַיְאַמֶּץ־ל֖וֹ בַּעֲצֵי־יָ֑עַר נָטַ֥ע אֹ֖רֶןוְגֶ֥שֶׁם יְגַדֵּֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: To cut down for himself cedars, and he took a holm-oak and an oak, and he let it grow strong for himself among [the] trees of [the] forest; he plants a pine, and rain makes [it] grow.

en.L: To cut down cedars for himself, he takes a holm oak or an oak and lets it grow strong for himself among the trees of the forest; he plants a pine, and [the] rain makes [it] grow.
en.B: He sets out to cut down cedars. He picks a holm oak or an oak and leaves it to grow strong among the forest trees. He plants a pine, and the rain makes it grow tall.
en.R: He goes out to cut down cedar trees. Or he chooses an oak tree and lets it grow strong among the trees in the forest. Or he plants a pine tree, and the rain makes it grow.

decisions.choice: holm oak, pine: trees whose exact kind is uncertain
decisions.reason: The first word occurs only here; it is a tree with hard wood, perhaps the holm oak or a cypress. The second is the Septuagint's 'pine' (described from memory; reviewer to check); others suggest a laurel or a fir.

decisions.choice: the rain makes it grow: the wood itself comes from God's care
decisions.reason: The man plants the tree, but the rain that God sends makes it grow (55:10). The idol maker depends on the Creator even for the wood of his god.

decisions.choice: an oak tree
decisions.reason: Readable names one familiar tree instead of two kinds of oak.

source.text: וְהָיָ֤ה לְאָדָם֙ לְבָעֵ֔ר וַיִּקַּ֤ח מֵהֶם֙ וַיָּ֔חָם אַף־יַשִּׂ֖יק וְאָ֣פָה לָ֑חֶם אַף־יִפְעַל־אֵל֙ וַיִּשְׁתָּ֔חוּ עָשָׂ֥הוּ פֶ֖סֶל וַיִּסְגָּד־לָֽמוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it becomes for a man for burning, and he takes from them and warms himself; also he kindles a fire and bakes bread; also he makes a god and bows down; he makes it an idol and prostrates himself to it.

en.L: And it becomes [fuel] for a person to burn, and he takes some of them and warms himself; he also kindles [a fire] and bakes bread; he also makes a god and bows down; he makes it an idol and falls down before it.
en.B: It is wood for people to burn. He takes some of it and gets warm; he lights a fire and bakes his bread. Then he makes a god as well, and bows down to it; he carves an idol and falls on his face before it.
en.R: People use wood like this to make fires. A man takes some of the wood to keep himself warm. He also uses it to start a fire and bake bread. Then he makes a god out of the same wood, and he worships it. He makes an idol and bows down to it.

decisions.choice: also ... also: the same wood serves for fuel and for a god
decisions.reason: The repeated 'also' brings out the absurdity: one log heats the oven and becomes the god he worships (verses 16-17, 19).

decisions.choice: bows down, falls down: acts of worship
decisions.reason: Both verbs describe bowing low before a god. The second is used in Isaiah only for bowing to idols (44:17, 19; 46:6).

source.text: חֶצְיוֹ֙ שָׂרַ֣ף בְּמוֹ־אֵ֔שׁ עַל־חֶצְיוֹ֙ בָּשָׂ֣ר יֹאכֵ֔ל יִצְלֶ֥ה צָלִ֖י וְיִשְׂבָּ֑ע אַף־יָחֹם֙ וְיֹאמַ֣ר הֶאָ֔ח חַמּוֹתִ֖י רָאִ֥יתִי אֽוּר׃

records.literal_gloss: Half of it he burns in fire; over half of it meat he eats; he roasts a roast and is satisfied; also he warms himself and says, Aha, I am warm, I have seen fire.

en.L: Half of it he burns in [the] fire; over [the other] half of it he eats meat; he roasts a roast and is satisfied. He also warms himself and says, "Aha! I am warm; I have seen [the] fire!"
en.B: He burns half of it in the fire. Over that half he cooks meat and eats; he roasts his meat and is full. He warms himself as well, and says, "Aha! I am warm; I can see the flames!"
en.R: He burns half of the wood in the fire. He cooks meat over it and eats until he is full. He warms himself and says, "Ah! I am nice and warm. I can see the fire!"

decisions.choice: half of it ... over half of it: the same half that burns cooks his meal
decisions.reason: The text may mean one half burns and the other half cooks, but verse 19 shows that it is the same fire: half the wood serves for warmth and food, the rest for the idol (verse 17).

decisions.choice: I have seen the fire: I feel the warmth of the blaze
decisions.reason: 'See' here means to enjoy or experience, as often in Hebrew. The man is content with his fire.

source.text: וּשְׁאֵ֣רִית֔וֹ לְאֵ֥ל עָשָׂ֖ה לְפִסְל֑וֹ יִסְגָּד־ל֤וֹ וְיִשְׁתַּ֨חוּ֙ וְיִתְפַּלֵּ֣ל אֵלָ֔יו וְיֹאמַר֙ הַצִּילֵ֔נִי כִּ֥י אֵלִ֖י אָֽתָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And the remainder of it into a god he makes, into his idol; he prostrates himself to it and bows down and prays to it and says, Deliver me, for my god [are] you.

en.L: And the rest of it he makes into a god, into his idol; he falls down before it and bows down and prays to it, and says, "Deliver me, for you [are] my god!"
en.B: What is left he makes into a god, an idol of his own. He falls down before it and worships; he prays to it and says, "Rescue me, because you are my god!"
en.R: He uses the rest of the wood to make a god, his own idol. He bows down to it and worships it. He prays to it and says, "Save me! You are my god!"

decisions.choice: deliver me, you are my god: words that belong to the LORD alone
decisions.reason: The man says to a piece of wood what Israel says to the LORD (Psalm 31:15; 140:7). The idol cannot deliver (45:20; 46:7).

decisions.choice: he falls down: the spelling of the verb differs between the written and the read text
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text and the vowels read with them give two forms of the same verb. The meaning is the same.

source.text: לֹ֥א יָדְע֖וּ וְלֹ֣א יָבִ֑ינוּ כִּ֣י טַ֤ח מֵֽרְאוֹת֙ עֵֽינֵיהֶ֔ם מֵהַשְׂכִּ֖יל לִבֹּתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: They do not know and do not understand, for [it] is smeared from seeing, their eyes, from having insight, their hearts.

en.L: They do not know, and they do not understand, for their eyes are smeared over so [they can]not see, their hearts so [they can]not understand.
en.B: They do not know, they do not understand; their eyes are smeared shut so they cannot see, and their hearts so they cannot grasp the truth.
en.R: People who worship idols do not know or understand anything. It is as if their eyes are covered so they cannot see. Their minds are closed so they cannot understand.

decisions.choice: their eyes are smeared over: the blindness of 6:9-10
decisions.reason: Isaiah was told that the people's eyes would be smeared over and their hearts dull (6:10, with the same verb). The idol makers suffer the blindness that idolatry brings (Psalm 115:8).

decisions.choice: it is smeared: the one who smears is not named
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject. It may mean that God has closed their eyes, as in 6:10, or simply that their eyes are shut.

decisions.choice: hearts: minds, the seat of thought and understanding
decisions.reason: In Hebrew the heart is where a person thinks and decides, not only where he feels.

decisions.choice: People who worship idols; It is as if
decisions.reason: Readable names who 'they' are and marks the smeared eyes as a picture.

source.text: וְלֹא־יָשִׁ֣יב אֶל־לִבּ֗וֹ וְלֹ֨א דַ֥עַת וְלֹֽא־תְבוּנָה֮ לֵאמֹר֒ חֶצְי֞וֹ שָׂרַ֣פְתִּי בְמוֹ־אֵ֗שׁ וְ֠אַף אָפִ֤יתִי עַל־גֶּחָלָיו֙ לֶ֔חֶם אֶצְלֶ֥ה בָשָׂ֖ר וְאֹכֵ֑ל וְיִתְרוֹ֙ לְתוֹעֵבָ֣ה אֶעֱשֶׂ֔ה לְב֥וּל עֵ֖ץ אֶסְגּֽוֹד׃

records.literal_gloss: And he does not bring back to his heart, and not knowledge and not understanding to say, Half of it I burned in fire, and also I baked on its coals bread; I roast meat and eat; and the remainder of it into an abomination will I make? To a product of a tree will I prostrate myself?

en.L: And he does not bring [it] back to his heart, and [there is] no knowledge and no understanding to say, "Half of it I burned in [the] fire, and I also baked bread on its coals; I roasted meat and ate. And the rest of it shall I make into an abomination? Shall I fall down before a block of wood?"
en.B: He does not think it over. He lacks the knowledge and the sense to say, "I burned half of it in the fire; I baked bread on its coals too; I roasted meat and ate. And am I to turn what is left into an abomination? Am I to bow down before a lump of wood?"
en.R: He does not stop and think. He does not have the knowledge or the sense to say, "I burned half of the wood in the fire. I baked bread on its coals. I roasted meat and ate it. Should I make the rest of it into something God hates? Should I bow down to a block of wood?"

decisions.choice: bring back to his heart: stop to think about it
decisions.reason: The phrase means to consider or reflect (46:8). The man never pauses to see what he is doing.

decisions.choice: abomination: something God finds detestable
decisions.reason: The word is used for idols and for practices the LORD hates (Deuteronomy 7:25-26; 27:15).

decisions.choice: a product of a tree: a mere block of wood
decisions.reason: The phrase is mocking. What he worships is just something that grew on a tree.

source.text: רֹעֶ֣ה אֵ֔פֶר לֵ֥ב הוּתַ֖ל הִטָּ֑הוּ וְלֹֽא־יַצִּ֤יל אֶת־נַפְשׁוֹ֙ וְלֹ֣א יֹאמַ֔ר הֲל֥וֹא שֶׁ֖קֶר בִּימִינִֽי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: He feeds [on] ashes; a heart deceived has turned him aside, and he does not deliver his self, and does not say, [Is it] not a lie in my right hand?

en.L: He feeds [on] ashes; a deceived heart has turned him aside; and he does not deliver himself or say, "[Is there] not a lie in my right hand?"
en.B: He grazes on ashes. A mind that has been fooled has led him off course. He cannot rescue himself or ask, "Is this thing in my right hand not a fraud?"
en.R: He is like someone who tries to live on ashes. His mind has been tricked, and it has led him the wrong way. He cannot save himself. He will not ask, "Is this idol in my hand a lie?"

decisions.choice: he feeds on ashes: he lives on what is worthless
decisions.reason: The verb is used of animals grazing. Ashes are what is left of the fire (verse 19). The picture is of a man trying to live on what cannot feed him (Hosea 12:2). The verb could also mean 'he befriends ashes'.

decisions.choice: a lie in my right hand: the idol he holds is a fraud
decisions.reason: The 'lie' is the idol itself, held or carried in his hand. 'Lie' is a common name for idols (Jeremiah 10:14; 16:19).

decisions.choice: He is like someone who tries to live on
decisions.reason: Readable marks the ashes as a picture of what cannot give life.

source.text: זְכָר־אֵ֣לֶּה יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כִּ֣י עַבְדִּי־אָ֑תָּה יְצַרְתִּ֤יךָ עֶֽבֶד־לִי֙ אַ֔תָּה יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֹ֥א תִנָּשֵֽׁנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: Remember these, O Jacob, and Israel, for my servant [are] you; I formed you, a servant to me [are] you, O Israel; you will not be forgotten by me.

en.L: Remember these [things], O Jacob, and Israel, for you [are] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant. I formed you; you [are] a servant to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, O Israel; you will not be forgotten by {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: Keep these things in mind, Jacob, and you, Israel, for you are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant. I shaped you; you are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own servant, Israel. You will never slip from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mind.
en.R: People of Israel, remember these things. You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant. I made you. You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant, Israel. I will never forget you.

decisions.choice: you will not be forgotten by me: God will not forget Israel
decisions.reason: The verb form with its ending is unusual. It most likely means that God will not forget his people (49:14-15). The Septuagint has 'do not forget me' (described from memory; reviewer to check), turning the line into a warning to Israel.

decisions.choice: these things: what was just said about idols and their makers
decisions.reason: Israel is to remember that the idols are nothing and that the LORD alone made them (verses 9-20).

source.text: מָחִ֤יתִי כָעָב֙ פְּשָׁעֶ֔יךָ וְכֶעָנָ֖ן חַטֹּאותֶ֑יךָ שׁוּבָ֥ה אֵלַ֖י כִּ֥י גְאַלְתִּֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: I have wiped out like the cloud your transgressions, and like a cloud your sins; return to me, for I have redeemed you.

en.L: I have wiped out your transgressions like a cloud, and your sins like a mist. Return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, for I have redeemed you.
en.B: Like a cloud I have wiped away your rebellious acts, and your sins like a mist. Come back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; I have redeemed you.
en.R: I have taken away your sins. They are gone, like a cloud that disappears. Come back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, because I have rescued you.

decisions.choice: like a cloud, like a mist: sins removed as clouds vanish
decisions.reason: Two words for cloud are used. As morning clouds melt away, so God has removed his people's sins completely (43:25; Hosea 6:4).

decisions.choice: return to me, for I have redeemed you: forgiveness comes first, and the call to return follows
decisions.reason: God does not wait for the people to return before he redeems them. He has already acted, and so he calls them back (43:1).

decisions.choice: transgressions: acts of rebellion
decisions.reason: The word means breaking faith with God, rebelling against him (1:2; 43:25, 27).

source.text: רָנּ֨וּ שָׁמַ֜יִם כִּֽי־עָשָׂ֣ה יְהוָ֗ה הָרִ֨יעוּ֙ תַּחְתִּיּ֣וֹת אָ֔רֶץ פִּצְח֤וּ הָרִים֙ רִנָּ֔ה יַ֖עַר וְכָל־עֵ֣ץ בּ֑וֹ כִּֽי־גָאַ֤ל יְהוָה֙ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וּבְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יִתְפָּאָֽר׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Shout for joy, O heavens, for [the] LORD has done [it]; shout, O lower parts of [the] earth; break forth, O mountains, [into] a shout of joy, O forest and every tree in it; for [the] LORD has redeemed Jacob, and in Israel he will glorify himself.

en.L: Shout for joy, O heavens, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has acted; shout aloud, O lower parts of the earth; break out, O mountains, [into] a shout of joy, O forest and every tree in it! For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has redeemed Jacob, and in Israel {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will show {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory.
en.B: Ring out with joy, you heavens, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has acted! Raise a shout, you depths below the earth! Burst into joyful song, mountains, you forest too, and every tree within it! For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has redeemed Jacob, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will show {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory in Israel.
en.R: Sky, sing for joy! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has done this. Deep places of the earth, shout! Mountains, forests and every tree, burst into happy songs! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has rescued the people of Israel. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will show how great {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is by what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does for them.

decisions.choice: lower parts of the earth: the depths beneath, set against the heavens above
decisions.reason: The heavens and the depths name the whole of creation, from highest to lowest (Psalm 148:7). Here it does not mean the world of the dead.

decisions.choice: has acted: God has done what he promised, without saying what
decisions.reason: The verb has no object. The end of the verse says what God has done: he has redeemed Jacob.

decisions.choice: he will show his glory: God displays his beauty and honor
decisions.reason: The verb means to show one's splendor. God's glory is seen in what he does for Israel (49:3; 60:21).

decisions.choice: by what he does for them
decisions.reason: Readable says how God shows his glory in Israel.

source.text: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ גֹּאֲלֶ֔ךָ וְיֹצֶרְךָ֖ מִבָּ֑טֶן אָנֹכִ֤י יְהוָה֙ עֹ֣שֶׂה כֹּ֔ל נֹטֶ֤ה שָׁמַ֨יִם֙ לְבַדִּ֔י רֹקַ֥ע הָאָ֖רֶץ מֵאִתִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says [the] LORD, your Redeemer, and [the one who] formed you from [the] womb: I [am the] LORD, [who] makes all, [who] stretches out [the] heavens by myself, [who] spreads out the earth; who [was] with me?

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, your Redeemer, and the one who formed you from [the] womb: I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who makes all [things], who stretched out [the] heavens by {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}, who spread out the earth by {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}},
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, your Redeemer, who shaped you in the womb, says this: I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who made everything, who alone stretched out the heavens, who hammered out the earth with no one beside {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}},
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says. He is the one who rescues you. He formed you before you were born. He says: I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I made everything. I stretched out the skies with no one to help {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I spread out the earth all by {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}.

decisions.choice: by myself: the reading of the margin (qere) is followed
decisions.reason: The written text can be read as a question, 'Who was with me?'. The marginal reading, followed here, says 'from with myself', that is, by myself. Both mean that no one helped God make the world (40:13-14).

decisions.choice: spread out: beat out flat, like a sheet of metal
decisions.reason: The verb describes hammering metal thin (40:19), and it is related to the word for the 'expanse' of the sky in Genesis 1:6. God shaped the earth as a smith shapes metal, unlike the smith of verse 12, who shapes an idol.

decisions.choice: who makes, who stretches, who spreads: a long description of God that runs through verse 28
decisions.reason: A string of descriptions of the LORD begins here and continues to the end of the chapter, ending with Cyrus and Jerusalem.

source.text: מֵפֵר֙ אֹת֣וֹת בַּדִּ֔ים וְקֹסְמִ֖ים יְהוֹלֵ֑ל מֵשִׁ֧יב חֲכָמִ֛ים אָח֖וֹר וְדַעְתָּ֥ם יְשַׂכֵּֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: [Who] frustrates [the] signs of empty talkers, and diviners he makes foolish; [who] turns back wise [men] backward, and their knowledge he makes foolish.

en.L: who frustrates [the] signs of empty talkers and makes diviners look foolish, who turns wise [men] back and makes their knowledge foolish,
en.B: who brings to nothing the omens of the babblers and makes the diviners look like fools, who sends the wise into retreat and makes their knowledge foolishness,
en.R: I make the signs of false prophets fail. I make fools of those who claim to tell the future. I make wise people look stupid. I show that what they know is foolish.

decisions.choice: empty talkers: those who make empty boasts or false predictions
decisions.reason: The same word appears in Jeremiah 50:36 for Babylon's false prophets. It may name a group of oracle-priests or simply people who talk nonsense.

decisions.choice: diviners: people who claimed to read the future from signs
decisions.reason: Babylon was famous for reading omens in the stars, in livers of animals, and in other signs (47:12-13). Divination was forbidden in Israel (Deuteronomy 18:10).

decisions.choice: frustrates the signs: God makes their predictions fail
decisions.reason: The LORD's word comes true (verse 26) while the forecasts of diviners do not. This is the test set in verse 7.

source.text: מֵקִים֙ דְּבַ֣ר עַבְדּ֔וֹ וַעֲצַ֥ת מַלְאָכָ֖יו יַשְׁלִ֑ים הָאֹמֵ֨ר לִירוּשָׁלִַ֜ם תּוּשָׁ֗ב וּלְעָרֵ֤י יְהוּדָה֙ תִּבָּנֶ֔ינָה וְחָרְבוֹתֶ֖יהָ אֲקוֹמֵֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: [Who] establishes [the] word of his servant, and [the] counsel of his messengers he fulfills; who says of Jerusalem, She will be inhabited, and of [the] cities of Judah, They will be rebuilt, and her ruins I will raise up.

en.L: who confirms the word of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant and fulfills the counsel of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} messengers, who says of Jerusalem, "She will be inhabited," and of the cities of Judah, "They will be built, and her ruins I will raise up,"
en.B: who makes good the word of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant and carries out the plan announced by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} messengers, who says of Jerusalem, "People will live in her again," and of the towns of Judah, "They will be built again; I will restore her ruins,"
en.R: I make the words of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant come true. I do what {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} messengers say I will do. I say about Jerusalem, "People will live there again." I say about the towns of Judah, "They will be rebuilt. I will build up the ruins."

decisions.choice: his servant: here the prophet who speaks God's word
decisions.reason: Set beside 'his messengers', the servant here is most likely the prophet, or prophets as a group, whose words God makes come true. Elsewhere in these chapters the servant is Israel (verse 21).

decisions.choice: her ruins: the ruins of Jerusalem, or of the land
decisions.reason: 'Her' is feminine singular. It most likely refers to Jerusalem, though it may mean the ruins of the whole land of Judah.

decisions.choice: Jerusalem inhabited and rebuilt: the city ruined by Babylon
decisions.reason: Babylon destroyed Jerusalem and its temple in 586 BC (2 Kings 25:8-10). The promise looks to its rebuilding after the exile (Ezra 1-6).

decisions.choice: my servant; my messengers
decisions.reason: Readable continues God's speech in the first person, as in the verses before.

source.text: הָאֹמֵ֥ר לַצּוּלָ֖ה חֳרָ֑בִי וְנַהֲרֹתַ֖יִךְ אוֹבִֽישׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: Who says to the deep, Be dry, and your rivers I will dry up.

en.L: who says to the deep, "Be dry, and your rivers I will dry up,"
en.B: who says to the ocean depths, "Dry up! I will make your rivers run dry,"
en.R: I say to the deep waters, "Dry up! I will make your rivers dry."

decisions.choice: says to the deep, Be dry: God's power over the waters, as at the Red Sea
decisions.reason: The LORD dried up the sea so his people could cross (Exodus 14:21-22; Isaiah 50:2; 51:10). Here the same power prepares for a new rescue. The rivers may also hint at Babylon's river, the Euphrates (Jeremiah 50:38; 51:36).

decisions.choice: the deep: the depths of the sea
decisions.reason: The word means the deepest waters (Jonah 2:4).

source.text: הָאֹמֵ֤ר לְכ֨וֹרֶשׁ֙ רֹעִ֔י וְכָל־חֶפְצִ֖י יַשְׁלִ֑ם וְלֵאמֹ֤ר לִירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ תִּבָּנֶ֔ה וְהֵיכָ֖ל תִּוָּסֵֽד׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Who says of Cyrus, My shepherd, and all my desire he will fulfill, and to say of Jerusalem, She will be built, and [the] temple, You will be founded.

en.L: who says of Cyrus, "My shepherd, and all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} desire he will fulfill," and to say of Jerusalem, "She will be built," and [of the] temple, "You will be founded."
en.B: who says of Cyrus, "He is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} shepherd; he will carry out everything I desire," and the word goes out about Jerusalem, "She will be built again," and to the temple, "Your foundations will be laid."
en.R: I say about Cyrus, "He is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} shepherd. He will do everything I want him to do." And the word will go out about Jerusalem, "It will be rebuilt," and to the temple, "Your foundations will be laid."

decisions.choice: Cyrus: Cyrus the Great, king of Persia
decisions.reason: Cyrus founded the Persian empire and took Babylon in 539 BC. In his first year he allowed the Jews to return to Judah and rebuild the temple in Jerusalem (Ezra 1:1-4; 2 Chronicles 36:22-23). The passage presents his naming as proof that the LORD declares the future before it happens (verses 7-8; 45:4).

decisions.choice: my shepherd: a ruler appointed by God to lead and care for a people
decisions.reason: Kings were called shepherds of their people (2 Samuel 5:2; Jeremiah 23:1-4). God calls a foreign king his shepherd, the one who will carry out his plan. In 45:1 he calls him his anointed.

decisions.choice: and to say: the words about Jerusalem may be God's or Cyrus's
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says 'and to say'. It may continue God's words ('who says ... and says'), or explain what Cyrus will do when he fulfills God's desire: he will order Jerusalem and the temple rebuilt (Ezra 1:2-3; 6:3).

decisions.choice: you will be founded: words addressed to the temple
decisions.reason: The verb form can be read as 'you will be founded', spoken to the temple, or as 'she will be founded', continuing the words about Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: the word goes out
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the infinitive 'to say' without naming the speaker, so that both readings in m3 stay open.
